transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’m here because I’m absolutely certain there are serious problems and hidden manipulations in the data at work, but no one believes me and it’s starting to cost me my job. I have pointed out the patterns to my colleagues repeatedly, but they just brush it off and act like I'm the one making things up.

During this time, have you also had periods of feeling unusually high or irritable with much less need for sleep, lots of energy, or feeling especially powerful or important? Or has it mainly been this fixed belief about the problems at work?

No, I haven't felt high or powerful at all; it's actually been the exact opposite. I feel completely drained, low on energy, and I've mostly withdrawn from my friends and hobbies. My mind is just entirely consumed by finding these data manipulations at work.

Have you been hearing voices or noticing things others don’t, or have people told you that your speech or behavior seems confused or disorganized? Aside from your beliefs about the data at work, has anything like that been happening?

No, I haven't heard any strange voices or seen things that aren't there, and no one has told me my speech or behavior is confused. My mind is perfectly clear, and my only concern is the very real manipulation of the data at my job.

Aside from this belief about the data at work, are you generally able to manage your daily life normally, like taking care of yourself, handling responsibilities, and getting along with people? Or has your functioning become impaired in other areas too?

It's actually been severely impacted, and my firm even suggested I take a leave of absence because my work has slipped so much. I've completely stopped seeing my friends or going to my hiking and star-gazing groups, which has put a massive strain on my marriage. I mostly just sit at home in silence, staring at these printouts and barely talking to my wife.

Over the same period, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day, with things like loss of interest, poor sleep or appetite, guilt, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living? Did these depressive symptoms start before or around the same time as your belief about the data manipulation?

I don't feel depressed, guilty, or suicidal, and my sleep and appetite are generally fine, though I did lose interest in my hobbies and withdrew from everyone about two years ago. That lack of energy and withdrawal started way before my realization about the data manipulation, which only became clear and strong over the last couple of months.

Before your belief about the data manipulation began, did you already have a long period of reduced emotions or expression, speaking much less, or having trouble motivating yourself to do everyday tasks? Or was it mainly just losing interest in hobbies and seeing people?

Yes, the loss of interest in hiking and seeing friends definitely started first, going back about two years ago when that big consulting project began. Over those two years, I became so consumed by checking the data that I gradually stopped talking much, lost my energy, and felt very little emotion, long before I became certain of the active manipulation a couple of months ago.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with schizophrenia, paranoid subtype, based on a persistent persecutory/delusional belief about data manipulation plus prominent negative symptoms (social withdrawal, reduced speech, low emotional expression, avolition/low energy) that clearly preceded the delusion and caused marked functional decline. There is no evidence of mania, prominent depressive syndrome, hallucinations, or disorganized speech/behavior sufficient to favor a mood or other psychotic disorder.
